elements.name: question23
elements.html:
Opening 

 

Acne is a very common inflammatory skin disease affecting approximately 231 million people globally. A key reason for acne development is a bacteria known as C. acnes. Treatments such as antibiotics and topical treatments target C. acnes but is limited by their severe side effects.

 

Currently, there is no vaccine that is approved for the treatment of acne which is why Sanofi have developed a vaccine against C. acnes as a potential new treatment.

elements.name: question27
elements.html:
Study Design

 

This is a Phase 1/2 first-in-human trial, and the aim is to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the vaccine at different dose levels. Approximately 260 participants will be enrolled into this study. 

 

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three cohorts. The treatment that you receive will be dependent on the cohort you are allocated to. Some participants will receive the study vaccine, and some participants will be receiving a placebo. The study is double-blinded which means neither you nor the study doctors will know what treatment you are receiving

 

Your initial screening visit will consist of another eligibility check with the doctors and blood tests, for which you should allow up to around 2-3 hours of time for. The first visit after this screen will be approximately 3-4 hours. You can also expect your subsequent follow-up visits to take around 1-2 hours

elements.name: question38
elements.html:
Study schedule and visits (Main Cohort B)

 

The study will last about 10 months with 18 planned visits. You will receive 3 vaccinations, on Day 1, Day 57 and Day 113.

 

  • Screening Visit (Day -29 to Day -1). The screening period is up to 29 days. During this visit, we'll do some initial tests to ensure you meet the criteria to participate in the study.
  • Visit 1 (Day 1). You will receive the first vaccine.
  • Visit 2 (Day 4)
  • Visit 3 (Day 8)
  • Visit 4 (Day 29/Month 1)
  • Visit 5 (Day 57/Month 2). You will receive the second vaccine.
  • Visit 6 (Day 60)
  • Visit 7 (Day 64)
  • Visit 8 (Day 85/Month 3)
  • Visit 9 (Day 113/Month 4). You will receive the third vaccine.
  • Visit 10 (Day 116)
  • Visit 11 (Day 120)
  • Visit 12 (Day 141/Month 5)
  • Visit 13 (Day 169/Month 6)
  • Visit 14 (Day 197/Month 7)
  • Visit 15 (Day 225/Month 8)
  • Visit 16 (Day 253/Month 9)
  • Visit 17 (Day 281/Month 10). 

 

To summarise, there will be 2 visits in the 7 days post vaccination, and then monthly follow up visits until the end of study. 

The follow up visits will include physical examinations, blood samples for safety assessments and may also include collection of facial skin swabs. 

 

Participation in this research is voluntary. If you don’t wish to take part, you don’t have to. You will receive the best possible care whether or not you take part.

elements.name: question40
elements.html:
Reimbursement:

You will be reimbursed $355 for each completed visit.

 

This totals to $6390 if you attend each scheduled visit.

elements.name: question90
elements.html:
Disclosure

 

Before we go any further, I want to explain exactly how the reimbursement works, so there are no surprises for you later. The reimbursement I just went through is what you'd receive if everything goes ahead as planned. That can look a bit different depending on what happens on the day. For example, if the doctor looks over your information early on and finds you're not eligible before you even get to the consent form, if you decide not to sign the consent form yourself, or if something doesn't line up with what you've told me today, you'd likely only get a partial amount, or in some cases nothing, instead of the full reimbursement.

 

That's actually a big part of why it matters that you're as accurate as possible with me right now. The doctor's early review is based on exactly what you tell me today, so the more accurate you are, the better your chances of making it all the way through screening and getting the full reimbursement.

elements.name: question45
elements.html:
That was all from me regarding the study information, did you have any questions for me?

 

 

Before we go on, please keep in mind that if you aren't successful for a screening this time, we do have other studies that you might be eligible for.  We also have a referral program where you can earn up to $250 for referring people for any of our studies. Are you happy for us to continue into the medical questions?

elements.name: question41
elements.html:
Extra info: 

 

  1. Has there been another acne vaccine developed before?

Yes, a similar vaccine targeting C. acnes was developed and tested in a Phase 1 first-in-human trial in 2021. The overall safety profile result of that study was favourable with no safety concerns identified. Sanofi acquired the company which developed that vaccine. 

 

2. What are the benefits or risks to participating in this study?

Since this is a first-in-human study, the benefits and risks at the individual level are unknown. There are risks associated with the vaccine component of the study, but there are also risk management tests that will be done to ensure your safety on the study. For example, the follow up visits to monitor any reactions 7 days after vaccination.

  • Testosterone therapy, enhancers or booster supplements
  • Vitamin B12 doses higher than 500μg/day if oral

 

Within 12 weeks of first study dose:

  • Cryodestruction (eg. cryotherapy)
  • Chemidestruction (eg. trichloro acetic acid)
  • Abrasion methods
  • Acne scar surgery (eg. microneedling)
  • Chemical peels
  • Photodynamic therapy
  • Light-based therapies (eg. laser, infrared)
  • Radiofrequency devices
  • Therapeutic ultrasound devices
  • X-ray therapy

elements.name: Referral
elements.title: Before we wrap up, I’d like to share details about our referral program. If you refer someone to us you can receive up to $250 if they enrol and participate in the study. Would you like to hear more?

elements.name: referral explanation
elements.html:
Great! Here's how it works:

 

To refer someone, you will need to provide them with a unique referral ID. The person you refer will need to provide us this ID either when they sign up on our website, or when they speak to us over the phone. This ID is essential, as it ensures we can track and reimburse you for any referrals.

 

For each person you refer who comes in for an in-person screening visit, you'll receive $50. If they go on to enrol and participate in the study, you'll earn an additional $200.

 

There's no limit- you can refer as many people as you'd like, as long as you have an exisiting relationship with them. It's important to note that you cannot advertise for referrals. This program is based on personal connections, so please only refer people you know.

 

If you're interested, we can set up your Unique Referral ID today if you would like (the unique referral ID is REF[p number]. E.g., REFP14471)

 

Who do you know you might be interested in this trial? (if they don't know anyone for this trial, they can also refer someone to any other trial)

 

Would you like us to send you an email that you can forward on to them?
